references.text: John 3:13 also mentions that the Son of Man is the one who has ascended to heaven, creating a direct parallel to the question of seeing him ascend to the place where he was before.
In John 13:3, John confirms that Jesus knew he had come from God and was going back to God, which mirrors the theme of origin and return to heaven in John 6:62.
John 16:28 contains Jesus' own confirmation that he came out from the Father and is returning to the Father, a direct reference to the same movement mentioned in John 6:62.
In John 17:5, Jesus asks the Father to give him glory with himself, the glory he had with the Father before the world existed, emphasizing the preexistence and origin noted in John 6:62.
John 17:11 describes Jesus as going to the Father, which is the same action (ascending) that is central to the question in John 6:62.
In John 20:17, Jesus says he is ascending to the Father, a direct fulfillment of the prophecy about ascending to the place where he was before, as mentioned in John 6:62.
